title: VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action
lede: Sukeban Games’s bartending visual novel: pixel-art characters in a neon-lit bar in Glitch City, framed by a screen of dark, outlined interface panels.
summary: Pixel art in magenta, violet, and cyan, with monospace dialogue in framed dark panels. Sukeban Games, Venezuela, 2016.

source.label: Steam: VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action

made: 2016 (released 21 June 2016 for Windows, macOS, and Linux)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected eight 1920 × 1080 px screenshots from the Steam store listing (app 447530) in a scratch folder. The observations come from the two bar screenshots with the drink-mixing panel.

styles.note: Partial fit: a cyberpunk interface in pixel art. It has the dark ground, magenta and cyan neon, framed panels, and monospace text, but its tone is warmer and more comic than dystopian.
Clear: the whole game is drawn in coarse pixel art, with framed dialogue panels and bitmap-style type.

context: Wikipedia: “VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action … is a 2016 visual novel developed by Venezuelan studio Sukeban Games and published by Ysbryd Games.” It was first released for Windows, OS X, and Linux on 21 June 2016. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VA-11_Hall-A).

Wikipedia: “The game features a retro-futuristic look based on cyberpunk media, PC-98 games, and anime-inspired visuals.” Corruption and food shortages “run rampant” in Glitch City, where the bar is. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VA-11_Hall-A).
observed: The screen is a frame of near-black and dark violet panels with thin outlines and small notches along the top edge.
The left panel shows the bar in pixel art: magenta and violet walls, a blue neon logo reading “KIRIRIN Light”, a pink neon bottle, and two round cyan-and-red gauges.
At top right, “Cyberpunk Bartender Action” in thin pink type sits above “VA-11 HALL-A” in heavy italic pink capitals.

The mixing panel is a grid of outlined cells labelled “Adelhyde”, “Bronson Ext”, “Pwd Delta”, “Flanergide”, and “Karmotrine” in a monospace pixel font, with gray beveled buttons “Reset”, “Mix”, “Slot 1”, and “Slot 2”.
Dialogue appears in a black box at the bottom, with the speaker’s name in magenta or blue (“Dorothy:”, “Jill:”) and the text in white monospace.
interpretation: The game reduces the style to a few interface rules (dark panels, outlined cells, monospace labels, neon accents) and shows that they work at a low resolution.
Its beveled gray buttons and anime characters pull it toward [pixel art](style:pixel-art) and away from the strict HUD look.
borrow: Color the speaker’s name, not the message, when you put dialogue or log lines in neon on black.
Lay out controls as a grid of outlined cells, each with a short monospace label.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The game and its screenshots belong to Sukeban Games and its publishers. The screenshots were viewed on the Steam store page only.
